Mean Multitaper Spectrum of Several Binned Records (Chave 2019)

SpecMTMChaveMat.Rd

Multi-record counterpart to SpecACF(m, ...): m is a matrix of records already binned onto a shared regular grid (one row per bin, one column per record, NA = gap), the same representation SpecACF/BinTimeseries produce. The spectrum of each record is estimated with SpecMTMChave (i.e. Multitaper.jl's mdmultispec(), see there for credit and references) and the mean over records is returned.

Usage

SpecMTMChaveMat(m, bin.width = 1, nw = 4, k = 7, min_pts = 4, detrend = TRUE)

Arguments

m

A matrix of binned records, one row per bin and one column per record, with NA for empty bins.

bin.width

The bin width, the sampling interval of the rows of m.

nw, k

Time-bandwidth product and number of tapers, as for SpecMTMChave.

min_pts

Records (columns) with fewer populated bins than this are dropped.

detrend

logical; remove a linear trend (against bin index) from each record first, as SpecACF does.

Value

A spec object with freq, spec (mean over records), dof (summed over records), bin.width, rfreq and nrec.

Details

mdmultispec()'s frequency grid is sized from the number of non-missing points it is actually given, so two records with different gap fractions would otherwise come back on different frequency axes even though they share a bin width and time origin. This is fixed here by choosing each column's zero-padding factor nz so every column's FFT length pads out to the same target regardless of how many of its bins are populated, after which every record's spectrum lands on the same frequency axis and the mean spectrum across records is a plain elementwise mean (no SpecInterpolate needed). nz is solved exactly (accounting for mdmultispec's internal rounding up of the point count to even) rather than approximately, since an approximate nz can round to an off-by-one FFT length for some column lengths and not others.

Real (non-simulated) record sets can have some records with very few populated bins after binning, not enough for k well-concentrated tapers at bandwidth nw. k is capped per column (both by the standard 2 * nw taper limit and by the column's own point count); columns with fewer than min_pts points are dropped rather than crashing.

rfreq is the Nyquist frequency 1 / (2 * bin.width), matching the rfreq convention that the Stan model (s_n = 0.5 * sigma_noise_adj^2 / rfreq) was calibrated against: the local SpecACF() this pipeline originally used (before it was replaced by PaleoSpec::SpecACF() in March 2023) computed rfreq as exactly the Nyquist frequency. PaleoSpec::SpecACF()'s current rfreq is instead the full sampling frequency (about 1 / bin.width, computed as max(freq) before truncating to positive frequencies), nearly twice the value this model expects, which inflates fitted sigma_noise by about sqrt(2) to compensate. mdmultispec's own frequency axis already stops at Nyquist, so max(freq) here is already the right quantity with no correction.

Credit

The spectral estimator is the work of the authors of the Julia package Multitaper.jl, Charlotte L. Haley and Christopher J. Geoga (https://github.com/lootie/Multitaper.jl, GPL-2); this function is only a wrapper that calls it. If you use it, please cite Haley and Geoga (2020) as requested by the package, and Chave (2019) for the method.

References

Chave, A. D. (2019). Multitaper spectral analysis for irregularly sampled and gappy data. Geophysical Journal International, 218(3), 2165-2178. doi:10.1093/gji/ggz280

Haley, C. L. and Geoga, C. J. (2020). Multitaper.jl: A Julia package for frequency domain analysis of time series. Journal of Open Source Software, 5(55), 2463. doi:10.21105/joss.02463
